title: DSP in Looping Dimensions — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of DSP in Looping Dimensions' rich face, its first round at Sketch tier: three made pieces that each walk up to a test of a claim the page makes (two combs against a torus scan, coupled plucked loops snapping or sliding, a dense lattice against noise), and two proofs and a plot gathered from the pages that already tested the rest, with the fingerprint of the words each was laid against. I grow when the page is rewritten or a piece has something new to test; I never hold the entry's words.

pieces.file: /Projects/2D Torus Wavetable Synthesizer/2D Torus Wavetable Synthesizer — rich — the ratio gate.html
pieces.title: the ratio gate · from the 2D Torus face
pieces.caption: **The rational-ratio bullet, already on trial.** Made this round for the 2D Torus page's own face, gathered here because it tests this section's third bullet on a real torus scan: one circle, then two, then a ratio no fraction names, then the drag through 3 ⁄ 2. Its finding, from its maker and challenger, not re-measured here: a simple ratio closes the scan into one harmonic series, as the bullet says, but nothing locks and nothing jumps. Just off 3 ⁄ 2 each partial slides by m·δ, and 1.5 + 10⁻⁹ sounds as 1.5 does.
pieces.near: This is why standard wavetables are stuck producing harmonic spectra

pieces.title: the lattice read back · a Dissolutions proof, 2026-10-20
pieces.caption: **Count the fundamentals from the sound alone.** A proof made for Rank-N Lattice Analysis, gathered because it puts this paragraph's rank to a measurement: light points on the grid of whole-number pairs, play them through two generators, and hand only the audio to an analysis that finds the fewest generators explaining every partial. By its own account, at √2 it hands your points back at rank 2, and at 3 ⁄ 2 the rows fall onto one series and the rank drops to 1. Its own verdict bears on the word *independent*: with whole numbers allowed to grow without limit, any finite set of peaks is rank 1, so the rank is a property of the sound and a bound you choose. Gathered as built, notes box included, which keeps only on this Mac's live face.
pieces.near: The mathematical name for the lattice of reachable frequencies

pieces.file: DSP in Looping Dimensions — rich — two combs.html
pieces.by: the Maker · comb filters and a torus scan
pieces.title: two combs · four steps
pieces.caption: **Where do two combs put their lines?** One comb's peaks, two combs in a row, a torus scan at the same two rates, and last the measurement. Through the comb pair the lattice's mixed points m·f₁ + n·f₂ stand no higher than random frequencies (+0.6 dB against +1.6, the two series +24.6); the scan puts the same points +60.3 dB up. The comb pair's lattice is real but sits in time: its first thirty echoes land on j·T₁ + k·T₂ within 0.02 ms.
pieces.near: place their combined peaks on a 2D frequency lattice

pieces.file: DSP in Looping Dimensions — rich — snap or slide.html
pieces.title: snap or slide · five steps
pieces.caption: **Do coupled plucked loops snap?** One Karplus-Strong loop, then two apart at φ, then a knob that lets them hear each other, then plucks while it turns, and last the whole knob measured. They slide. At the steepest point of every reading, halving the notch halves the change (×0.50, then ×0.25), across two mixers, three ratios and two pitches. The lossless mixer reaches one harmonic series only at full swap; the crossfeed gets most of the way between c ≈ 0.17 and 0.33, an S-curve with a short-ringing middle. Both land on the series of one loop as long as both, f₁·f₂ ⁄ (f₁ + f₂): 84 Hz for 220 and 136.

pieces.title: where a snap does live · the 2D Torus coupled scan
pieces.caption: The contrast. Here the two scan phasors themselves are coupled, Kuramoto-style, on the Penrose surface at ratio 1.518 pulled to 3 ⁄ 2: as coupling ramps from 0 to 1.6 Hz, the slip rate falls and the lock and the harmonicity jump together at 0.80 Hz. A snap, because phase dynamics are nonlinear; the plucked loops beside it are linear, and slide. Rendered by the 2D Torus steward (Tools/kuramoto_scan.py).

pieces.file: DSP in Looping Dimensions — rich — listen longer.html
pieces.by: the Maker · a scan on T^N, and noise
pieces.title: listen longer · four steps
pieces.caption: **Does it ever become noise?** One loop's lines, loops added up to six at golden, plastic, silver and other irrational rates, noise beside the tone, and last the measurement: the share of energy in the loudest tenth of bins as the window grows from 21 ms to 5.5 s. Noise never moves (34.5 to 36.2 %). The tone always pulls away, but slower with every loop: two loops reach 99.9 % by 0.68 s, six only 51.2 % by 5.5 s. The limit holds; how long you listen decides when it shows.
pieces.near: It can be made arbitrarily rich by adding dimensions

offers.what: "N loops at irrational ratios ⇒ N independent fundamentals, plus every integer combination of them" holds when the loops are read together through one table, as a torus scan reads them. Loops that only filter or add give each loop's own harmonics and nothing between. Measured in the two-combs piece: through two combs in a row at 220 and 220 ⁄ φ Hz, the sixteen mixed points m·f₁ + n·f₂ a scan's surface carries stand +0.6 dB above the band's median bin, the same as 400 random frequencies (+1.6 dB), while the two series stand +24.6 dB; the scan puts those sixteen points +60.3 dB up. Proposed: "…plus, when the loops are read together through one table, every integer combination of them; loops that only add or filter keep each one's own harmonic series."

The third bullet's "the system 'phase-locks'": in a scan with a fixed rational ratio nothing locks; the lattice folds onto one series because m·f₁ + n·f₂ = (m·p + n·q)·f₂ ⁄ q. Locking names a dynamic, which Frame 3 calls up, and this round's snap-or-slide piece finds none in coupled plucked loops either. The 2D Torus face's ratio-gate piece (its maker and challenger, not re-measured here) found the fold is a slope by ear: just off 3 ⁄ 2 each partial slides by m·δ. Proposed: "the scan closes" for "the system 'phase-locks'".

Frame 2: two combs at an irrational ratio do not give "exactly the same spectral signature as toroidal scanning". Measured in the two-combs piece (a = b = 0.95, T₁ = 1 ⁄ 220 s, T₂ = φ ⁄ 220 s, six seconds of noise through both): the pair's peaks are the lattice's two axes, k ⁄ T₁ and l ⁄ T₂ (+24.6 dB above the median bin); its mixed points sit at the noise floor (58 points with |m|, |n| ≤ 6: −0.3 dB; random frequencies +1.6 dB); a torus scan at the same rates puts its mixed points +60.3 dB up. A linear filter only reshapes the frequencies it is given; m·f₁ + n·f₂ needs a product (a table read at two phases, a ring modulator, a nonlinearity). The pair's 2D lattice is in time: its echoes land on j·T₁ + k·T₂, the first thirty within 0.02 ms. Proposed: "Two combs with periods T₁ and T₂ at irrational ratio put their peaks on the lattice's two axes, and their echoes on a 2D lattice in time, j·T₁ + k·T₂ — the frequency-time rhyme of toroidal scanning, which fills the lattice between the axes." The same holds for "N coupled delay lines … spectral support on an N-dimensional lattice": coupled, the modes leave the axes but do not land on the lattice either (see the Frame 3 offer).

Frame 3: coupled plucked loops slide; they do not snap. Measured in the snap-or-slide piece on two Karplus-Strong loops at 220 and 220 ⁄ φ Hz (ρ = 0.996), with two mixers, a crossfeed [1 − c, c; c, 1 − c] and a lossless rotation by c·90°: at the steepest point of the distance-from-one-series reading and of the spectral change, halving the notch halves the change (×0.50, then ×0.25) in all twelve runs (golden, √2 and π ⁄ 2 ratios, 220 and 330 Hz, both mixers). Lossless: the distance falls 0.44 → 0.02 in a near-straight line and the series is reached only at c = 1; its modes are the roots of cos(πf(T₁ + T₂)) = cos(c·π⁄2)·cos(πf(T₂ − T₁)), matched by the rendered pluck within 0.03 Hz. Crossfeed: an S-curve, 0.56 → 0.01, most of it between c ≈ 0.17 and 0.33, with the middle ringing 0.4 to 1 s against 6.4 s apart. Both land on the series of one loop as long as both, f₁·f₂ ⁄ (f₁ + f₂) (84 Hz here), lower than either loop, not on a common subdivision. Why: plucked loops are linear and damped, and nothing in them is a self-sustaining oscillator, which Kuramoto locking needs; the snap the palace has measured is between coupled scan phasors (2D Torus, Penrose, 0.80 Hz). Proposed: "Couple the loops and the modes slide from two harmonic series toward one, the series of a single loop as long as both, f₁f₂ ⁄ (f₁ + f₂), reached when the mixer fully swaps them. Bell to string is a morph here; a Kuramoto snap needs oscillators that sustain themselves, as in the coupled scan of the [[2D Torus Wavetable Synthesizer]]." Untested here: whether bowed (self-sustaining, saturating) loops snap.

"always a discrete, finitely-generated lattice in frequency space": finitely generated, yes; discrete, no. Once two rates are at an irrational ratio, the frequencies m·f₁ + n·f₂ are dense on the frequency line (Kronecker's theorem, the one the page's epigraph alludes to). Computed for 220 and 220·φ Hz: the nearest to 300 Hz is 4.03 Hz away with whole numbers up to 20, 0.65 Hz up to 100, 0.033 Hz up to 1000. What keeps the spectrum from noise is that it is a countable sum of single frequencies (pure point), not that it is discrete. Proposed: "always a finitely generated set of single frequencies: countable, dense on the frequency line once two rates are irrational, but never a continuous spread", and "discrete and lattice-structured" → "made of lines, lattice-structured".

An addition: the limit holds in the mathematics, and how long you listen decides when it shows. Measured in the listen-longer piece, share of a 100–4000 Hz band's energy in its loudest tenth of bins, windows 21 ms to 5.5 s: noise 34.5 to 36.2 % at every window; one loop past 99 % by 43 ms; two loops 99.9 % by 0.68 s; six loops 40.7 % at 21 ms, rising unevenly to 51.2 % at 5.5 s. With six loops, 136,862 lines within 60 dB of the loudest fall in that band, against 21,299 bins in a 5.5 s window. Proposed, after "remains discrete and lattice-structured": "The more loops, the longer one must listen before the lines part: with six, a five-second listen cannot part them all."
